problem: Fixed-bucket pruning (bucket_start = (now // window) * window, drop q[0] < bucket_start) replaces the (now - window, now] sliding window, so up to 2×limit requests are accepted across any bucket boundary (limit=2, window=10: t=9,9.5,10,10.5 all accepted vs main's T,T,F,F), float floor division misplaces boundaries (window=0.1 accepts two requests 4e-17s apart at limit=1), and the class is still named SlidingWindowLimiter.

retry_after still returns q[0] + window - now (sliding-window math) while allow now resets at bucket_start + window, so it overstates the wait and disagrees with allow (retry_after(3)=8.0 yet allow at t=10 succeeds).

The rewritten line keeps unbounded growth of _accepted (read-only remaining/retry_after insert entries for unseen keys and empty deques are never removed, so client-controlled keys grow memory without bound) and adds a per-call __import__('collections').deque() allocation instead of the imported deque.
from collections import deque is now unused because line 23 switched to __import__, so ruff check fails with F401.

The repository has no tests, so the bucket-boundary regression and retry_after/allow disagreement went undetected; one boundary test (limit=2, window=10, t=9,9.5,10,10.5 → T,T,F,F, retry_after(10.5)=8.5) would catch them.

_observe accepts non-finite now: nan disables the time-went-backwards check and permanently locks a key, and inf makes the branch's retry_after return -inf (main returned 0.0) before bricking the limiter.
The comment documenting the window contract (now - window, now] was deleted in the same change that altered the semantics, leaving the window's meaning undocumented.
